haiku-low.q1: The API checks the unfiltered reports.row_count from the replica. At 10,000 or fewer rows it streams the CSV in the response, which the browser saves. Above that, it queues a job and returns HTTP 202. The user gets an email with a link.
haiku-low.q2: The request returns the existing active export with HTTP 200 and starts no new one. The response says which filters that export uses, so changed filters are not applied.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed signed link works for 24 hours. The bucket deletes the file 7 days after creation. No cleanup job exists. The page's download endpoint issues a fresh 24-hour link.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts, with queue waits of 60 and 300 seconds. After the third failure, the row is set to failed with an error, and a failure email is sent. The user can then click Download CSV again.
haiku-low.q5: Report rows are read only from the read-only replica, never from the primary database.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports row, its only record. The page polls GET .../exports/latest every 5 seconds while queued or running. Reopening the page calls the same endpoint and shows the latest state.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000 rows at a time by keyset from the replica, encodes them as CSV into a 5 MB buffer, and uploads each full buffer as a multipart part. At most about 10 MB is held. Whether a 900 MB run fits in 30 minutes is unmeasured.
haiku-low.q8: Uploaded parts stay in storage but are invisible until completion. The next attempt aborts the open upload, discarding them, and restarts from the beginning with the same payload. Open uploads are discarded within 24 hours.
haiku-low.q9: Filters and columns are copied into the report_exports row when the user clicks. The job payload holds only export_id, so the job reads filters and columns from that row.
haiku-low.q10: A unique database index on (user_id, report_id), applied only to queued or running rows. The losing insert fails, and that request returns the active export.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be complete: upload completed, object_key and row_count saved, status done. If the job reruns after email_sent_at is set, it stops. If done but unsent, it only sends the email.
haiku-low.q12: The response simply stops, so the browser saves a partial file and the user is not told. This happens on a database failure or the 60-second limit. Errors before the first byte return a normal error response.

sonnet.q1: Step 2 reads reports.row_count (unfiltered total) from the replica. 10,000 or fewer: small path, CSV streamed in the same response (text/csv, attachment) with header row. More than 10,000: large path, a report_exports record is created and a job queued (HTTP 202 with export ID, status queued); a worker builds the file and the user gets an email with a download link.
sonnet.q2: The server returns the existing active export with HTTP 200 and creates no new one, even if the URL filters changed. The response should say which filters that export uses.
sonnet.q3: The emailed signed link works 24 hours (86400 seconds). The exports bucket deletes each file 7 days after creation (no cleanup job is built). The page can get a fresh link via the download endpoint while the file exists.
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts (waits 60s before attempt 2, 300s before attempt 3). After the third fails, the failure handler aborts any open upload, sets status to failed with a short error message, then sends a failure email using the failure template. The page shows failed and the error; the user can click Download CSV again.
sonnet.q5: The replica (read-only copy); report rows are never read from the primary.
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports table row (the only place status is kept). The page polls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest every 5 seconds while queued or running, stopping at done or failed. On reopening, the same request returns the latest export's state.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads 5,000 rows at a time from the replica by keyset, encodes to CSV into a 5 MB buffer, uploads each full buffer as a multipart part (keeping ETags), then uploads the remainder as the final part. Memory is about 10 MB at most regardless of report size, and nothing is kept on disk. The document does not give timing for 2 million rows; the largest (about 900 MB) is unmeasured against the 30-minute limit.
sonnet.q8: Nothing half-written is visible, since the file appears only when the upload is completed in step 6. The open upload is aborted by the next attempt (step 3) or discarded by the bucket after 24 hours. The next attempt restarts from the beginning (no progress kept), starting a new multipart upload.
sonnet.q9: They are copied from the URL into the filters and cols columns of the report_exports row at click time. The job payload holds only {"export_id": ...} and the job loads the row to read them.
sonnet.q10: A database unique index on (user_id, report_id) applied only to rows with status queued or running. If an insert violates it, the loser returns the active export.
sonnet.q11: The file must be complete (upload completed, object_key and row_count saved, status done) before the signed link is created and emailed; email_sent_at is set after sending. On a rerun: if the row is done and email_sent_at is set, the job stops; if done but email_sent_at is empty, it skips to step 7 and just sends the email.
sonnet.q12: If it fails before the first byte, a normal error response is returned. If the database fails or the 60-second limit runs out partway, the response just stops, the browser saves a partial file, and the user is not told (open question 2). No export record or file exists.
